questions.stem: What role do decomposers play in the nitrogen cycle?

options.text: They convert nitrogen gas into nitrates
They break down dead organisms and waste, releasing ammonia into the soil
They absorb nitrates from the soil for growth
They convert nitrates back into atmospheric nitrogen

questions.explanation: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organisms and animal waste, converting the proteins and urea into ammonia. This ammonia can then be converted into nitrites and nitrates by nitrifying bacteria.
